slides.title: Page structure
slides.html:
HTML

Page structure

  • An element = opening tag, content, closing tag
  • <head>: info for the browser (title, CSS)
  • <body>: everything people see
  • Attributes add extra info: lang, href, src
  • In VS Code, type ! then Tab to get this

index.html

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport"
      content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>My first page</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  </head>
  <body>
    <h1>Hello, BlockHub!</h1>
    <p>This is my first web page.</p>
  </body>
</html>

slides.title: Semantic tags
slides.html:
HTML

Semantic tags

  • Semantic tags say what content is, not how it looks
  • header, nav, main, section, article, footer
  • They help screen readers and Google understand your page
  • <div> is a box with no meaning: use it only for styling

index.html

<body>
  <header>
    <nav>
      <a href="#about">About</a>
      <a href="#contact">Contact</a>
    </nav>
  </header>
  <main>
    <section id="about">
      <h2>About me</h2>
    </section>
    <article>A blog post</article>
  </main>
  <footer>© 2026 Ada</footer>
</body>

slides.title: Text, links, images and lists
slides.html:
HTML

Text, links, images and lists

  • h1 to h6: headings, one h1 per page
  • p: paragraphs; strong and em for emphasis
  • a: links, with href
  • img: images, with src and alt (no closing tag)
  • ul bullets, ol numbers, li items

index.html

<h1>Main title</h1>
<h2>Section title</h2>
<p>A paragraph with <strong>bold</strong> and
  <em>italic</em> text.</p>
 
<a href="https://blockhubglobal.xyz">Visit BlockHub</a>
<a href="#contact">Jump to contact</a>
 
<img src="images/me.jpg" alt="Ada smiling at her desk">
 
<ul>
  <li>HTML</li>
  <li>CSS</li>
</ul>

slides.title: Selectors: choosing what to style
slides.html:
CSS

Selectors: choosing what to style

  • A rule = selector { property: value; }
  • Link it in the head: <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  • Classes (.card) are what you will use most
  • When rules clash, the more specific wins: id, then class, then element

style.css

/* element */
p { color: #333; }
 
/* class: reuse on many elements */
.card { padding: 24px; }
 
/* id: one element only */
#hero { min-height: 100vh; }
 
/* descendant + hover */
nav a { text-decoration: none; }
nav a:hover { color: #00ff66; }

Full-Stack Development · Week 1 · HTML & CSS

slides.title: Colours and typography
slides.html:
CSS

Colours and typography

  • Colours: names, hex #00ff66, rgb(), hsl()
  • CSS variables let you reuse colours everywhere
  • Get free fonts from Google Fonts
  • rem = size relative to the root (16px by default)
  • line-height 1.5 to 1.7 keeps text easy to read

style.css

/* reusable colours */
:root {
  --green: #00ff66;
  --dark: #050605;
}
 
body {
  font-family: "Plus Jakarta Sans", sans-serif;
  font-size: 18px;
  line-height: 1.6;
  color: #222;
}
 
h1 { font-size: 3rem; color: var(--dark); }

slides.title: The box model
slides.html:
CSS

The box model

margin

border

padding

content

Every element is a box: content, then padding, border and margin around it.

style.css

.card {
  width: 300px;
  padding: 24px;          /* inside the border */
  border: 2px solid #ddd;
  margin: 16px auto;      /* outside the border */
}
 
/* width now includes padding and border */
* { box-sizing: border-box; }

slides.title: Flexbox: one direction
slides.html:
Layout

Flexbox: one direction

  • Lays items out in a row or a column
  • justify-content: spacing along the row
  • align-items: alignment across it
  • gap: space between items
  • Perfect for navbars, buttons and rows of cards
Logo
Home
About
Contact

style.css

.navbar {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between; /* along the row */
  align-items: center;            /* across the row */
  gap: 24px;
}
 
.cards {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 16px;
}
.card { flex: 1 1 250px; }

slides.title: CSS Grid: rows and columns
slides.html:
Layout

CSS Grid: rows and columns

  • Grid controls rows and columns at once
  • fr = one share of the free space
  • Flexbox for one direction, Grid for two
1
2
3
4
5
6

style.css

.gallery {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  gap: 20px;
}
 
.layout {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 250px 1fr; /* sidebar + main */
}
 
.hero { grid-column: 1 / -1; }   /* full width */

slides.title: Design for the phone first.
slides.html:
Responsive design

Design for the phone first.

Many of your visitors will open your site on a phone. Start with one simple column, then add layout as the screen gets wider.

Full-Stack Development · Week 1 · HTML & CSS

slides.title: Media queries
slides.html:
Responsive design

Media queries

  • Keep the viewport meta tag in your head (it is in the starter)
  • A media query is CSS that only applies above a width
  • Use %, fr and rem instead of fixed widths
  • Test in DevTools device mode: Ctrl + Shift + M

style.css

/* phones first: one column */
.cards { display: grid; gap: 16px; }
 
/* tablets and up */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .cards { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }
}
 
/* laptops and up */
@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .cards { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); }
}
 
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }

slides.title: Websites for everyone
slides.html:
Accessibility

Websites for everyone

Alt text

Describe every image for screen readers. Decorative images get alt="".

<img src="me.jpg"
  alt="Ada coding">

Headings in order

One h1, then h2, h3. Never pick a heading just for its size.

h1 → h2 → h3

Contrast

Text must stand out from its background: at least 4.5:1.

#777 on white ✗
#333 on white ✓

slides.title: The HTML
slides.html:
Build · step 1

The HTML

  • Get the content right before styling
  • Use semantic tags for each part
  • Give a class to anything you will style
  • The full file is in your notes

<header>
  <nav class="nav">
    <a href="#" class="logo">Ada.dev</a>
    <a href="#projects">Projects</a>
    <a href="#contact">Contact</a>
  </nav>
</header>
<main>
  <section class="hero">
    <h1>Hi, I'm Ada. I build websites.</h1>
    <a href="#contact" class="btn">Work with me</a>
  </section>
  <section id="projects" class="projects">
    <article class="card">Project one</article>
  </section>
</main>

slides.title: The CSS
slides.html:
Build · step 2

The CSS

  • Reset first: box-sizing and margins
  • Flexbox for the navbar
  • Grid for the projects
  • One media query for wider screens

* { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; }
body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
 
.nav {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  padding: 20px 5%;
}
.hero { min-height: 80vh; display: grid; place-items: center; }
.projects { display: grid; gap: 20px; padding: 5%; }
 
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .projects { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); }
}

slides.title: Recap and homework
slides.html:
Wrap-up

Recap and homework

You can now…

  • Build a page with semantic HTML
  • Add text, links, images, lists, forms and tables
  • Style it with selectors, colours and fonts
  • Lay it out with the box model, Flexbox and Grid
  • Make it responsive and accessible

Homework

  1. Finish your landing page with at least 5 sections
  2. Test it at 375px, 768px and 1280px in DevTools
  3. Push it to GitHub and publish it with GitHub Pages
  4. Submit your live link on BlockHub before next class
